probe_assessment: The cold-read probe held up. Its purpose and all four public API descriptions match the module: cuts are detected on the 288p scale-only downsample, precomputed court-view votes classify cut-to-cut segments, the returned mask uses True for dead frames, and the CLI saves the mask. It reported no stumbles, and the module does not contain a material code-caused comprehension trap for the listed points.

verdicts.claim: Docstring sentence violates the rule 'no more than a single sub-clause per sentence' by combining multiple dependent clauses and parenthetical reasoning.
verdicts.quote:
Fail loud on an all-dead result: no live segment means nothing for the
segmenter to anchor to (apply_replay_mask rejects an all-True mask anyway), so
a fully-dead mask is almost always a bad vote input rather than a real answer.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Split into simpler sentences: 'Fail loud on an all-dead result: no live segment means nothing for the segmenter to anchor to. The apply_replay_mask function rejects an all-True mask anyway. A fully-dead mask is almost always a bad vote input rather than a real answer.'
verdicts.verifier_note: The quote is verbatim at lines 105-107. It is one long sentence with a colon, a parenthetical clause, and a concluding 'so' clause, which exceeds the rubric's single-sub-clause guidance for docs-prose.
